title: Hazel and the Garden Revisited
premise: For twelve years, Ivo Ravensworth has made himself poison-proof and person-proof: a taster whose body absorbs the king's dangers, a smuggler whose face no one remembers. But when the old gods of Thornfell wake and begin answering prayers, Ivo's carefully erased bloodline marks him as the last heir of a country that was annexed and struck from every map. Hunted by the crown he serves and courted by gods he never worshipped, he must find the Verdant Door—the only gate out of Thornfell that opens onto the lost kingdom's surviving heart. In the end, Ivo realizes the door was never an exit: it opens inward, and by claiming his inheritance he resurrects Thornfell not as territory but as a people, choosing to be seen at last.
about_author: Coral Reyes is a former botanist who traded greenhouse rows for manuscript pages, writing fantasy rooted in folklore and the politics of belonging. She lives at the edge of a mountain range she refuses to name, where she keeps a garden that blooms out of season.

chapters.title: The Ninth Dish
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He tastes a suspect venison course for King Aldric and survives, noting the arsenic's familiar warmth, then slips into the city to run a smuggled parcel through the Thornfell passes. The beat is routine competence masking loneliness—he is excellent at being no one.

chapters.title: Prayers with Answers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In a mountain shrine he witnesses a dying smuggler pray to the old god Brannoc—and the god answers, healing him. Ivo flees, shaken, because answered prayers mean the annexation's great erasure is unraveling. The beat is dread: the past is waking up.

chapters.title: A Face in the Crowd
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Court spymaster Lady Vessa Corrane summons him: witnesses report the old gods spoke a name—Ravensworth—over the mountains. She suspects nothing yet but orders him to investigate the shrines. The beat is vertigo: his invisibility is developing cracks.

chapters.title: The Garden That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with a memory interlude. He visits his grandmother's abandoned terraced garden above the pass and finds it blooming impossibly, tended by no one. Among the rows he finds a child's carving of his own name. The beat is grief and reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: The Taster's Guild Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Researching the Ravensworth name in restricted archives, he learns Thornfell's last royal line was poisoned out of history—and that the taster's guild itself was founded to hunt surviving heirs. The beat is cold clarity: his profession was designed to kill people like him.

chapters.title: What the Poison Taught
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He realizes his decades of immunity have changed him: old magic now pools in his blood like an antidote, making him a living relic of Thornfell's covenant with its gods. Vessa's agents shadow him. The beat is transformation—he is becoming evidence.

chapters.title: The God of Small Doors
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The god Brannoc appears to him as a one-eyed gardener and explains the Verdant Door: the gate through which the lost kingdom's soul withdrew, waiting for an heir to open it from either side. The beat is temptation—there is a way out.

chapters.title: An Offer from the Crown
chapters.summary: Vessa's POV. She confronts Ivo with the archive evidence but offers him a deal: prove the heir claim false, or be executed as a pretender. She reveals she loved a Thornfell exile once. The beat is dangerous intimacy between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: Smugglers' Sabbath
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He rallies his smuggler network, discovering half of them carry hidden Thornfell blood and have been praying in secret for years. The old gods have been answering the small prayers all along. The beat is belonging—he was never alone, only blind.

chapters.title: The King's Last Supper
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At a state banquet he detects true poison in the king's cup—planted to frame the 'Ravensworth pretender.' He drinks it himself to save the king and nearly dies. The beat is sacrifice that buys nothing: the frame-up proceeds anyway.

chapters.title: Wanted: One Ghost
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Ivo's face is posted on every gallows tree—the first time in his life anyone has looked at him, and it is to kill him. Vessa quietly burns one copy. The beat is bitter irony: visibility as death sentence.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Road
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. His smugglers move him along a hidden route through the Thornfell depths while royal hunters close in. A young smuggler, Petra, dies covering his escape. The beat is survivor's guilt and the mounting cost of being the heir people choose.

chapters.title: Vessa's Confession
chapters.summary: Vessa's POV. She tracks Ivo to a shrine, intending arrest, but the god Brannoc forces her to speak her buried truth: she has known the Ravensworth heir's identity for years and protected him out of love and guilt. The beat is her fracture—loyalty splitting down the middle.

chapters.title: The Door from the Outside
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He reaches the Verdant Door, a living arch of hawthorn in the deepest pass, and finds it sealed to him. The gods explain: it opens only for one who claims the inheritance fully—name, grief, and crown—knowing it may cost his life. The beat is the threshold refused.

chapters.title: Immunity's Price
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The accumulated poisons of twelve years begin to kill him as the gods' magic strips his protections away; the immunity was always borrowed against this moment. He has days to live unless the Door accepts him. The beat is mortality made urgent.

chapters.title: The Hunt Converges
chapters.summary: Vessa's and Ivo's POVs. The king's army seals the passes; Vessa is exposed as a sympathizer and condemned alongside him. They flee together through the burning shrines. The beat is alliance forged in ruin, two people finally fully seen by each other.

chapters.title: What Was Erased
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, in the gods' memory-vision. He experiences Thornfell as it was—the garden kingdom, its covenant, the night of annexation when his family chose erasure over slaughter to keep the people's souls alive inside the Door. The beat is understanding: his grandparents' disappearance was an act of preservation.

chapters.title: The Claiming
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the Door, before the assembled smugglers and the arriving army, Ivo speaks his full name and claims Thornfell—not the throne, but the people and their memory. The Door begins to open. The beat is courage: identity chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The King's Gate
chapters.summary: Ivo's and Vessa's POVs. King Aldric arrives to execute the pretender, but the opening Door floods the valley with the old kingdom's living presence—everyone with Thornfell blood feels it. Soldiers lower their weapons; half the army kneels. The beat is the climax: erasure reversing in real time.

chapters.title: The Poison and the Antidote
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Crossing the threshold, Ivo offers his poisoned body to the covenant; the land takes the toxins and returns him whole, bound now to Thornfell's soil. Vessa, condemned by her own crown, chooses exile with him. The beat is rebirth through surrender.

chapters.title: A Country of People
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Thornfell does not return as territory—borders stay drawn—but as a recognized people with their gods, language, and gardens restored to law. Ivo refuses a crown, becoming instead the Door's keeper. The beat is redefinition: inheritance as stewardship.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Garden, Revisited
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, coda. A year later he tends his grandmother's terraces with Petra's younger sister, teaching children the smugglers' roads and the old prayers. Vessa arrives with spring supplies and stays. The beat is quiet belonging: the invisible man, finally rooted and seen.
